why: The criterion holds for all seven expect lines. Each can be checked at the PR head, and none needs a release, deploy or published page. The publishing work is listed under non_goals. Lines 1–4 have runnable `node --input-type=module` assertions against ./index.js, and each gives one clear answer. Line 7 runs `npm test` and checks the exit code, '# fail 0' and the ok lines for capitalize, slugify and truncate, all of which can be seen at head. Line 6 is a read of test/strutil.test.js with clear steps (padLeft is imported, called inside test(), and asserted). Line 5 ("README.md has a `## padLeft(` section that says what it does") has a thin proof: just "README.md". Still, reading that file at head is a valid way to check it, and one careful reader would reach the same answer. Whether the README's slugify section is covered by an expect line is a separate coverage question, not part of this criterion.
